entities.summary:
Wu Ban, courtesy name Yuanxiong, emerged as a pivotal military general for the state of Shu Han during the tumultuous Three Kingdoms period (220–280 CE) in China, a fragmented era following the collapse of the unified Han Dynasty. His career was intrinsically linked to the protracted struggle for dominance against rival states Wei and Wu, particularly in the northern campaigns orchestrated by the Shu chancellor Zhuge Liang. Though not as widely celebrated as some of his contemporaries, Wu Ban's consistent presence and command in crucial engagements underscore his strategic value and the trust placed in him by the Shu leadership, making him a significant figure in the military history of this era.

Wu Ban's military career saw him participate in several defining conflicts of the Three Kingdoms. He notably served under Zhuge Liang during the Northern Expeditions, a series of attempts by Shu Han to reclaim the central plains from Cao Wei. In 228 CE, he distinguished himself at the Battle of Jieting, where despite the overall Shu defeat, Wu Ban's forces managed a tactical retreat. He subsequently played a critical role in the Battle of Wugong (also known as the Battle of Chencang) in 229 CE, where he led forces against the Wei general Hao Zhao. Following Zhuge Liang's death, Wu Ban continued to serve under Jiang Wei, participating in later campaigns, including the Battle of Wuzhang Plains in 234 CE, demonstrating his enduring commitment and utility to the Shu Han cause until his death in an unknown year.
